style.vernacular: Dense mid-rise reinforced-concrete frame buildings with brick infill, plastered and painted in faded cream, ochre, pale green and pale blue, streaked by monsoon damp; flat roofs with water tanks and rebar stubs, window grilles and balcony rails; exposed red brick and raw concrete for the Kahn-era modernist public buildings; Mughal and colonial-era mosques and houses in Old Dhaka with plastered arches and small domes; tin-roofed informal sheds; mango, rain tree and banyan shade trees and palms.
style.ornament: Mughal-derived cusped arches, merlon parapets and small ribbed domes on old mosques; chinitikri broken-china mosaic (star and floral patterns) on domes and facades; colonial-era louvred shutters and verandahs; modern Bangladeshi modernism of exposed brick and concrete with large circular and triangular openings; hand-painted signboards.

sources.what: Dhaka as Mughal capital (Lalbagh Fort, Saat Masjid), Indo-Saracenic Ahsan Manzil, Curzon Hall, Louis Kahn modernism, concrete in the modern period
chinitikri china-tile mosaic facade and domes, Mughal style, small five-domed mosque
raised platform, three domes, cusped arches, merlon parapet, Mughal-period Dhaka mosque form
